cases.note: Without a server token the route answers 500 and never calls GitHub.
A plus sign in the query string is a space, which is not allowed.
Whitespace is present, so this is an invalid name, not a missing one.
39 characters is the longest GitHub login.
The name also travels as a GraphQL variable, never inside the query text.
The caller cannot choose the date range.
2025-10-12 is a Sunday; six days back is Monday 2025-10-06.
365 days back is already a Monday, so no further adjustment.
365 days, not one calendar year: 2024-02-29 is inside the window.
The range depends on the server's time zone. Here it is already 13 October locally, which changes the Monday chosen.
Still 12 October locally.
Noon local time is kept, so 'from' is 17:00 UTC in winter time while 'to' is 16:00 UTC in summer time.
02:30 local did not exist on 2025-03-09, the day 365 days back. JavaScript moves it to 03:30, and that hour is kept for the Monday.
01:30 local happened twice on 2025-11-02. The Monday chosen is unaffected.
A rejected SERVER token reaches the caller as 401, as if the caller were not signed in.
GitHub's status code is passed to the caller unchanged, with a fixed message.
GitHub reports an unknown login as an error, so the caller gets 400 'GraphQL query failed', never the 404 below. Reply shape follows GitHub's documented behaviour; not observed live.

errors.message: Could not resolve to a User with the login of 'no-such-user'.

cases.note: An empty errors list counts as a failure, because any list is truthy in JavaScript.
A reply that is not an object is reported as 'User not found'.
totalContributions is GitHub's number, not a sum. With no days the average is 0.
Each day gains its week and weekday position. The streak counts back from the newest day.
A day with no contributions yet ends the streak, even early in that day.
Days are ordered newest first by date before counting, whatever order GitHub sent. The grid keeps GitHub's order.
0.25 becomes 0.3. JavaScript's toFixed rounds a tie upward.
7/20 is stored as slightly less than 0.35, so it becomes 0.3.
9/20 is stored as slightly more than 0.45, so it becomes 0.5.
An average of exactly 2 is the number 2, not 2.0.
The shape of a day is not checked. A missing field is simply left out of the reply.
With no total the average is not a number, which JSON writes as null, and totalContributions is left out.

github_token_semantics: Per-user GitHub credential, verified with the matching Supabase session; never the server token.
